previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic pain consistent with a recurrent urinary tract infection, given his history of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and prior multidrug-resistant UTIs. He was started empirically on ciprofloxacin, which was confirmed appropriate when urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to ciprofloxacin. His pain improved over the hospital stay, and he completed three days of a seven-day antibiotic course at discharge. He experienced a brief episode of chest pain radiating to the jaw, but cardiac workup was reassuring with no enzymatic or EKG changes. His anxiety and depression were ongoing concerns; he expressed social withdrawal and fear of being alone, and was maintained on citalopram and duloxetine. Constipation was managed with an aggressive bowel regimen including lactulose. He was discharged to a rehab facility with plans for outpatient follow-up regarding antibiotic suppressive therapy, continuation of ciprofloxacin, and monitoring of mood, mobility, and bowel function.

#  Suprapubic pain: likely ___ to UTI with clouding urine and 
chronic indwelling foley which was due to be changed on ___.  
U/A with large Leuks, 139 WBCs.  Patient had BM last night after 
disimpaction and fleet enema, but chronic constipation still in 
ddx.  His foley was changed on ___, and he was started on 
Meropenem given his history of MDR organisms.  On ___ his cx 
showed mixed flora indicating chronic colonization.  He was 
discharged on Ciprofloxacin for a total of 7 days.  He was also 
continued on aggressive bowel regimen.  

# Penile ulcer: The ulcer on his penis was swabbed and purulent 
discharge cultured.  RPR, GC/Chlamydia, and HSV were negative.  
Wound cx was positive for sparse growth of MRSA, but this was 
thought to be secondary to culturing of superficial wound with 
skin colonization and was not treated.  Wound team was consulted 
and suggested cleansing, followed by antibacterial cream and 
covered with xeroform.  They also suggested f/u with urology 
which is scheduled for next week. 

# Hypotonic bladder/BPH - he was continued on home tolterodine. 
He will f/u with Urology as an outpatient upon discharge.

# Chronic Constipation - aggressive bowel regimen with 
senna/colace/bisacodyl/lactulose/milk of mag

# Right Kidney Mass - stable on prior imaging, thought to likely 
be due to RCC, but patient deemed not surgical candidate on 
prior admission.  Has f/u with urology next week.

Discharge Instructions:
Mr. ___, you were admitted to ___ after presenting with 
lower abdominal pain, and burning around your foley catheter.  
You were found to have a urinary tract infection and were treat 
with broad-spectrum antibiotics until the urine cultures showed 
that the infection was due to a several different bugs.  Your 
foley catheter was removed and replaced on ___.  You will be 
treated for 7 days with ciprofloxacin.  You will follow-up with 
your primary care physican and Urology next week for further 
treatment.

Your blood pressure was slightly low while you were in the 
hospital.  We stopped your lisinopril and you should have your 
blood pressure rechecked at your follow-up appointment before 
restarting this medication.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

Please see your follow-up appointments listed below.

You should take Tylenol every 8 hours for pain, whether or not 
you are having pain! You can also taken Naproxen as needed every 
8 hours for pain. We also provided you with a topical gel for 
pain.

It was a pleasure caring for you and we wish you a speedy 
recovery!
